page_header: Chemical Equilibrium, Acids and Bases · 4 marks

steps.label: The definition
lines: A buffer solution is a solution whose pH
changes very little when a small amount of
a strong acid or a strong base is added to
it, or when it is diluted.
Buffer solutions are of two types:
a) acidic buffer  b) basic buffer
steps.why: The definition has three test conditions — small added acid, small added base, dilution — and the buffer holds its pH nearly constant under all three. Naming the two types sets up the rest of the answer.
common_mistakes: Writing that the pH does not change at all. It changes very little, not zero.
Writing that a buffer works against ANY amount of added acid. The definition says a small amount.
steps.memory_tip: Three small changes — added acid, added base, dilution — and the pH stays nearly the same.
steps.margin_note: The two marks are for the full definition with 'small amount' in it.

steps.label: Acidic buffer
lines: Acidic buffer: a mixture of a weak acid and
its salt with a strong base. Its pH is
steps.why: The weak acid and its salt supply a conjugate acid-base pair in one solution — the acid can react with added base and the salt's anion with added acid, which is what keeps the pH nearly steady.
common_mistakes: Writing strong acid + its salt. A buffer needs the WEAK acid; a strong acid ionises completely and leaves no reserve.
Pairing the weak acid with a random salt. The salt must contain the acid's own anion (its salt with a strong base).
steps.memory_tip: Weak acid + its own sodium salt: acetic acid + sodium acetate is the standard pair.
steps.margin_note: The example pair CH₃COOH/CH₃COONa is expected by name.

steps.label: Basic buffer
lines: Basic buffer: a mixture of a weak base and
its salt with a strong acid. Its pH is

lines.text: Buffer = weak acid or weak base + its own salt; pH changes very little on small additions

steps.why: The basic buffer is the mirror of the acidic one: weak base plus its salt with a strong acid gives the conjugate pair on the basic side of 7.
common_mistakes: Writing NaOH + NaCl as a basic buffer. NaOH is a strong base; the buffer needs the weak base NH₄OH.
Swapping the salt types — the basic buffer's salt comes from a strong ACID (NH₄Cl).
steps.memory_tip: The basic pair is ammonia solution + ammonium chloride; the acidic pair is acetic acid + sodium acetate.
steps.margin_note: Box the one-line summary; both named pairs sit above it.

insider_note: Definition plus the two named mixtures — CH₃COOH with CH₃COONa and NH₄OH with NH₄Cl are the expected examples, and an answer without them loses the type marks.
